answer: Every new identity needs an invite-escrow sponsor: the inviter locks 1,500 POA in a contract naming the invitee for 180 days. The inviter signs a request binding their own ID to the fresh key. The contract records the lien and emits a public receipt anyone can audit. If the invitee sybils, that stake is burned; an honest inviter recovers principal when the clock expires. A farm of 1,000 clones costs 1.5 million POA plus the sponsor's standing, so the network sits on a ridge where each fake node drags its author down — a sonnet whose every stolen line burns the writer's crystal crown.
